clue.text: Get the bug, and make an unexpected loss?

definitions.meaning: to pick up a common infection such as a sniffle
in business slang, to lose money on a deal one expected to profit from

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom covers both falling ill with a minor infection and suffering a financial setback.

clue.text: Carefully inspect suit when entering church

indicators.note: entering means one piece goes inside the other, here the word for church taking in a short word

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Someone checks over a smart suit before going into church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' is a second definition (a lawsuit is a case), sitting beside the first: this clue defines its answer twice around the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Thieves case a joint, meaning they look it over carefully before a burglary.

clue.text: Monarch volunteers to inhale a nerve gas

indicators.note: to inhale means the first piece breathes in, so holds, the second

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
sarin is a nerve agent used as a chemical weapon

explanation.surface: A ruler's volunteer soldiers are made to breathe a nerve agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar's wife or a female tsar was a Russian empress, a kind of sovereign.

clue.text: Slide headlong

definitions.meaning: a spiral fairground chute ridden on a mat

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a tall spiral funfair chute and also means in confused haste.

clue.text: Interrupts demand for less immoral behaviour?

definitions.meaning: read as a command: reduce wrongdoing, i.e. trim wickedness

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into two words: an order to reduce sin.
explanation.definitionFit: To butt into someone's speech is to break in on them, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Rent by itself is much less

parts.note: to rent out a property is to let it
alone means on its own

explanation.surface: Rent paid on its own amounts to a much smaller sum.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as in 'I can't walk, never mind run', the phrase means still less or not to mention.

clue.text: Mark's causing alarm no end

indicators.note: no end means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: something scary causes alarm

explanation.surface: A mark on the skin is frightening, endlessly so.
explanation.definitionFit: A blemish left on the skin after a wound heals is a lasting mark.

clue.text: Arrive for work and notice unfinished unit

parts.note: to clock something is slang for noticing it

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: one is the unit number

explanation.surface: A worker turns up and spots a part-built unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers record their arrival time on a time clock, so the phrasal verb means start a shift.

clue.text: Very angry missing start of exciting sporting event

indicators.note: missing means a letter is left out of the phrase

parts.note: really cross means very angry

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone is furious at missing the opening of a thrilling sports fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor race over mixed tarmac and dirt circuits is a kind of sporting event.

clue.text: Type of onion: try eating every bit

indicators.note: eating means one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: a shot is an attempt or try
all means every bit

explanation.surface: A cook urges someone to try eating every bit of an onion.
explanation.definitionFit: A small mild bulb related to the onion, so a type of it.

clue.text: A kitchen aid can cook one's goose?

parts.note: a can is a tin
to cook someone's goose is to thwart them, to foil them

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget might be used for roasting a goose.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin metal sheet for wrapping food is a standard kitchen aid.

clue.text: Somewhat unattractive description of watercolour?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for someone rather plain-looking
taken literally, a watercolour is a picture made without oils

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for a plain person is read literally as describing a painting not done in oils.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom says someone is not good-looking, as a painted portrait would flatter them.

clue.text: Admire boy band's shape very much

parts.note: to like is to admire
Billy is a boy's name
a ring-shaped band looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A fan says they admire a boy band's look enormously.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal intensifier means intensely or with great vigour, as in 'raining hard'.

clue.text: Bit of a black eye? It can open

indicators.note: bit of means the letters are a piece taken from inside the words

explanation.surface: Part of a bruised eye might be able to open.
explanation.definitionFit: A key is the tool that opens a lock.

clue.text: Test team's bonus?

parts.note: a cricket or football side is an eleven
a plus is an advantage or bonus

explanation.surface: Is a test of the side a reward?
explanation.walkthrough: The ELEVEN-PLUS was the British exam taken at about eleven to decide entry to grammar school.
explanation.definitionFit: A school selection examination is a test.

clue.text: One in US city is eager, at first, to exchange information

indicators.note: in means one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: at first means take the opening letter only

explanation.surface: A keen person in an American city wants to swap news.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping in contact and sharing information with another party is the job of a go-between.

clue.text: Witticism about the Queen entertaining band

parts.note: on means about or concerning

indicators.note: entertaining means holding, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina
a line is a stripe or band

explanation.surface: A joke about Her Majesty hosting a musical group.
explanation.definitionFit: A quip delivered in a single sentence is a witticism.

clue.text: Chess champion from small county town

parts.note: Taunton is the county town of Somerset in England

explanation.surface: A chess winner comes from a little English county town.
explanation.walkthrough: Howard Staunton was the leading English chess player of the 1840s; the Staunton chess set is named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Howard Staunton was regarded as the world's best chess player in the 1840s.

clue.text: Feud may spell ruin for all in Mediterranean capital

indicators.note: putting one thing for another means substituting it in that place

parts.note: Valletta is the capital of Malta
taken as written
end means ruin or destruction

explanation.surface: A feud may bring disaster to everyone in a Mediterranean capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a long blood feud between families.

clue.text: Locals name a Cornish resort, but not initially

indicators.note: not initially means the first letter is removed

parts.note: St Ives is a seaside resort in Cornwall

explanation.surface: Residents name a Cornish seaside town, though not at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: People born in a place are its locals.

clue.text: Eccentric American cricket writer

parts.note: a card is an eccentric or amusing person
US means American

explanation.surface: An oddball from the States writes about cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: Neville Cardus was a celebrated English writer on cricket and music.
explanation.definitionFit: Neville Cardus wrote on cricket for the Manchester Guardian for decades.

clue.text: Lassie's heavenly body?

parts.note: Lassie the film collie was a canine screen celebrity, while the same phrase names Sirius in the night sky

explanation.definitionFit: Sirius is the brightest star in the constellation Canis Major, and Lassie was a famous animal film star.

clue.text: Laugh about leader of conga after end of energetic dance

indicators.note: after means this piece comes behind the earlier one
the end of a word is its last letter
about means surrounding, so the laugh goes round the other letter

parts.note: ha-ha is a laugh

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone chuckles at the conga leader after an energetic dance ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin American ballroom dance with a triple step.

clue.text: Enthusiast needing to get tight?

definitions.meaning: the threaded fastener screwed onto a bolt and tightened

explanation.definitionFit: A devotee is called a nut, and a nut is also the hardware screwed down tight on a bolt.

clue.text: Criminal count had shot is critical

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrong or mangled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a go is a shot or attempt

explanation.surface: A crooked aristocrat has been shot and is in a serious state.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means precarious or of uncertain outcome, a crucial moment.

clue.text: Bars used to make one in Greek island close to mainland?

indicators.note: in means the number one is placed inside the other letters
close to means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Barriers are used to make an island near the Greek mainland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'island' adds nothing to the letters; it builds the Greek-island picture behind the parse.
explanation.definitionFit: A grid is a framework of crossing bars, as on a grating.

clue.text: Fast runner, potentially, always allowed to go round

indicators.note: to go round means the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: let means allowed
ever means always

explanation.surface: A sprinter is always permitted to do another lap.
explanation.definitionFit: A young hare will grow into a fast runner, hence the 'potentially'.

clue.text: One shedding tears about that heartless animal in America

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a crier is someone who weeps

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letters are taken out

explanation.surface: A weeping person stands over a cruelly treated American animal.
explanation.definitionFit: US dialect for any living creature, a variant of 'creature'.

clue.text: A band from the south has reformed

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south

indicators.note: reformed means formed anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musical group from the south has got back together.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a long strip of cloth worn round the waist or over the shoulder.

clue.text: Put in jeopardy as grenade exploded next to border

parts.note: an end is a boundary or border

indicators.note: exploded means blown apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grenade went off by the frontier, putting people at risk.
explanation.definitionFit: To expose to danger is to put at risk.
